warnings_excerpt: [lob] lob: inning 9 top folded LOB 2 != inning_summary LOB 1
dispositions.evidence: OURS, NOT THE SOURCE'S. In the 9th top two runners are retired together on the half's terminal non-plate-appearance event. check_lob measures at the last plate appearance and reports 2; the true end state is 0; the source's Inning Summary says 1, matching neither. The source is not wrong here in a way an erratum could fix -- our rule is measuring at the wrong instant, and this is one of its eleven known misses.
dispositions.alternative_scored: The broadened rule -- also subtract runners retired on the terminal event -- was written and scored corpus-wide: it fires on 476 half-innings, recovers 2 and regresses 474, for 98.11% against the current rule's 99.96%. Correcting the source line instead would use the errata file to hide a limitation of our own oracle, which its docstring forbids outright.

dispositions.evidence: Marked final, 0-0 linescore, twenty boxscore rows totalling ZERO at-bats, and two events: a substitution and an Inning Summary claiming one runner left on base by a side that never batted. There is no game here to parse. parse_game refuses it at the source, requiring a page with panes to yield either a plate appearance or an unparsed line before it can become a final file.
dispositions.alternative_scored: Not a candidate for correction -- there is nothing to correct toward. The number worth recording is the one that makes this dangerous rather than trivial: it passed 5 of 5 replay oracles for the life of the corpus, because all 5 were written to find a disagreement and an empty game offers none. check_has_content (the 6th) exists because of it, and its own test asserts that the original five still pass on the empty game -- if one ever starts catching it, the sixth check can go.
